A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeepSPI work. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable, and retained content can be matched across renumbering and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original stochastic Atari experiments comparing DeepSPI, PPO, DeepMDP and DreamSPI, including learning curves and model-prediction losses.

after.justification: v2 reports original Atari results and statistical analyses, plus a new trained-agent maze experiment measuring returns and learned representation separation.

M1.justification: The neighborhood operator, DeepSPI's PPO-style clipped utility incorporating reward and transition losses, and DreamSPI's imagined-trajectory procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 2 corrects gradient subscripts to match the parameter groups already specified in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on a raw-pixel, two-branch maze designed to expose confounding policy updates (Section 6.1 and Appendix G). The existing stochastic Atari coverage is retained; the maze is a focused additional task.

E2.justification: PPO and PPO augmented with DeepMDP losses remain the Atari baselines, with DreamSPI retained as the planning variant. The new maze comparison reuses PPO. Added related-work citations and externally attributed runtime comparisons do not introduce evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 adds IQM, mean and optimality-gap summaries alongside medians. Its new maze protocol uses 84-by-84 observations, a 256-state discrete representation and tighter DeepSPI clipping. Existing Atari preprocessing, collection settings and the hyperparameters in Tables 1–2 remain substantively unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 6.1 adds a focused diagnostic case study tracking whether PPO and DeepSPI merge or separate the two critical maze states. Appendix H.2 extends the existing model-quality analysis with aggregate loss comparisons and statistical assessment. v1 already contained Atari loss curves and DreamSPI examples.

E5.justification: The reported Atari seed count increases from three to eight, and the stated per-environment bands change from 40–60% to the proper 25–75% interquartile range. v2 adds 95% stratified-bootstrap intervals, a paired bootstrap and Wilcoxon signed-rank test, plus ten-seed maze summaries.

E6.justification: Atari performance and loss curves are revised alongside the expanded seed count, and new aggregate results are reported. The maze yields returns around 8 for DeepSPI versus 4.8 for PPO. Appendix H.2 newly reports a DeepSPI-minus-DeepMDP mean transition-loss difference of -0.1381, a 95% interval of [-0.2226, -0.05907], and p = 0.00066.

T1.justification: Theorems 1–5 and their existing proofs remain substantively unchanged. New Appendix G formally defines the maze MDP and derives values for three policies. Numbering the previously stated episodic assumption does not itself introduce a new assumption.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: neighborhood-based improvement and convergence, world-model and representation guarantees, and a PPO-based algorithm competitive with PPO and DeepMDP. The additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 connects the maze's return differences to representation collapse or separation and interprets the transition-loss statistics as evidence against sampling noise. It also discusses the measured runtime overhead and explains computational advantages of architectural Lipschitz constraints. The existing discussion of DreamSPI's planning limitations is largely retained.

D1.justification: v2 discloses NVIDIA A40 hardware, per-algorithm runtime means and standard deviations, transition-density and loss-coefficient search ranges, and maze implementation details. These expand reproducibility information; the selected Atari hyperparameters were already present in v1 and remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 1.1 adds positioning relative to offline model-based methods including MOPO and COMBO, and connects the representation guarantees to state abstraction and bisimulation. Additional references support these connections and the statistical analyses, while the central online, representation-aware positioning is retained.

P1.justification: v2 adds a theoretical roadmap, changes much baseline-policy terminology to behavioral policy, makes the episodic assumption more explicit, and reorganizes the experimental appendices. It also updates affiliations and the publication header. Most existing prose and proof structure remain intact.

P2.justification: The experimental presentation is substantially expanded with maze diagrams, observation examples, representation curves and aggregate confidence-interval plots. The score learning curve switches to IQM, existing plots are redrawn, and v1's main-text relative-improvement chart moves to Appendix H as Figure 11. Tables 1–2 retain their structure.

improvement.justification: v1's empirical claims relied on three-seed plots with narrow 40–60% bands. v2 substantially strengthens their support through eight-seed results, corrected interquartile reporting, bootstrap confidence intervals and a paired transition-loss analysis. The maze supplies direct evidence of representation behavior in a specified setting, while runtime and search disclosures improve reproducibility. These changes address an important weakness in empirical reliability without relying on higher scores alone.
